Materials and light

The millwork is painted with a 2½" face frame and slim shaker doors with a ½" trim, the kind of quiet, tailored detail that lets the books and the art carry the room. Try the millwork across a grey to green range, from a deep charcoal through grey green and sage to a deep green. The counter and the window sill are solid wood to match the tone of the desk, so the oak runs as one line across the wall.

Every open shelf has a 2" thick front with 1" Hafele Loox 5 puck lights recessed into the underside, two per bay, so each shelf throws a soft scallop of light down the back panel and onto the pieces below. The shelf backs can match the millwork, go to white oak, or go dark navy so the lit shelves stand out; try them with the buttons above. The cabinet lights come on by motion or when a door opens. Art lights over the window, the built-in and the jerseys pick out the rest. A ½" shadow reveal runs at the base of every wall and where the cabinets meet the walls, so the joints stay crisp with no baseboard. The display wall finishes with its own stepped crown up to the ceiling.

The floor is the herringbone hardwood we chose for the lower level, which gives the room a bit of pattern under all that calm cabinetry.
